item.title: [6] Semiconductors pushed into insulator territory
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Hironori Okumura

Score 6/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Potentially relevant electronic properties and phase behavior in a semiconductor material.

Tags: #material #electronicstructure

Abstract: A material that was previously assumed to be an electrical insulator has been shown to be a semiconductor, with potential uses in electronics and optics.

item.title: [6] How to control where semiconductor crystals start growing
item.content:encoded:
Authors: Authors not available in source RSS

Score 6/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Material synthesis methodology for large single crystals relevant for spectroscopy samples.

Tags: #method #material #crystalgrowth

Abstract: Semiconductor crystals grow from tiny nuclei, but the position of these nuclei is difficult to control precisely and can affect the crystal’s properties. An approach using ‘etching flux’ has now been developed that constrains the position at which a nucleus forms, enabling spatially programmable growth of large single crystals of semiconducting material.

item.title: [8] A chiral superlattice route to spin-split topological antiferromagnetism
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Philip Kim, Su-Yang Xu

Authors: Thao Dinh, Mengke Liu, Jian-Xiang Qiu, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant topological antiferromagnet with anomalous Hall and Berry curvature features.

Tags: #topological #antiferromagnet #berry_curvature

Abstract: A chiral superlattice in collinear antiferromagnetic UOTe generates large Berry curvature and spin-polarized currents, enabling anomalous Hall effects and advancing chiral quantum materials for spintronics.
